title: arXiv Biology & Biomedicine — Notable Recent Papers — 2026-11-19
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. This is an inferred relevance-ranked selection from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a popularity ranking; bioRxiv, medRxiv, and the wider clinical literature are not covered.

sections.title: Headline
sections.abstract: Latest available announcement batch: Thursday, 19 November 2026. This report selects 13 papers, led by protein-structure and interaction evaluation, cross-modal molecular prediction, and computational cell dynamics. The agenda is to distinguish measurement from model prediction and identify needed validation. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance-ranked selection from incomplete biomedical coverage, not a popularity ranking.

sections.title: Biases and Limits of AlphaFold Predictions for Non-Globular Proteins
sections.abstract: The authors assemble experimentally validated non-globular protein cases to show how AlphaFold predictions can diverge from biologically relevant states when molecular context is missing.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors offer a framework for considering interactions and assembly, biological environment, global architecture/topology, and physical constraints when interpreting predicted structures.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a curated collection, not a systematic estimate of AlphaFold error rates. State selection often needs orthogonal experimental evidence, including NMR, SAXS, cryo-EM, or cross-linking.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper organizes 27 experimentally validated cases into four discrepancy classes; a Biology+AI Daily technical thread also discussed it, which is a discussion signal rather than a popularity measure.

sections.title: Cardiac MRI-informed electrocardiography enables biologically grounded cardiomyopathy detection
sections.abstract: MyoECG transfers CMR-derived structural and functional information into an ECG representation for cardiomyopathy detection from ECGs alone at inference.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report AUROCs of 0.800–0.974 across their datasets and improved mean reader sensitivity and specificity with model assistance.
sections.unique_caveat: Retrospective preprint evidence is not a prospective clinical-impact study. Case mix and prevalence varied; authors note limited positive predictive value in low-prevalence datasets and call for prospective validation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report 45,241 paired ECG-CMR examinations for pretraining, over 1.8 million ECGs across seven data sources, and a six-cardiologist reader study using 403 ECGs.

sections.title: ProteinGeoBench: Frontier Structural-Biology Agents Are Fluent at Lookup but Lost in Geometry
sections.abstract: ProteinGeoBench tests whether AI agents can retrieve facts about protein structures, check sequences, calculate coordinate geometry, and reason about structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report a gap between fact lookup and coordinate-based geometry, and show that rankings shift with network access and agent harness; the leaders were too close to order reliably under their bootstrap analysis.
sections.unique_caveat: Results concern a specific benchmark and tool setup, not general biological reasoning or experimental performance. Access and harness configuration materially affect scores.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The revised study includes 131 tasks, 4,249 runs across four frontier models, and a 26-model subset; benchmark tasks and code are publicly linked by the authors.

sections.title: SCOPE: Single-Cell Omics Prediction from Histology via RNA-Protein Prior Enhancement
sections.abstract: SCOPE combines gene-protein relationships and biological priors to predict cell-resolved RNA and protein profiles from H&E images, including markers without direct training labels.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a shared cross-omics model trained on unpaired assay sections and designed to extend predictions beyond directly supervised markers.
sections.unique_caveat: These remain computational predictions, not molecular assay replacements. External protein cohorts were limited in size (35 colorectal-cancer patients and 40 ORION patients), and correlation does not establish cell-level biological accuracy.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Tested across 16 organs and two external protein cohorts; authors report mean RNA-correlation gains of 8.8% and protein-correlation gains of 9.7% for seen and 11.9% for unseen markers against stated baselines.

sections.title: Are You Learning Biological Signal or Shortcuts? Auditing and Mitigating Bias in Protein-Protein Interaction Datasets
sections.abstract: The authors audit study and technical biases in protein-interaction datasets that can let machine-learning models exploit shortcuts rather than interaction biology.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a Nextflow pipeline using similarity-aware splits and optimization-based negative sampling to reduce selected dataset biases.
sections.unique_caveat: The analysis concerns the databases, splits, and negative-sampling procedures studied; mitigation of these shortcuts does not by itself establish accurate biological interaction prediction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The revision compares HIPPIE, IntAct, STRING, and two PDB-derived datasets, and reports distinct shortcut signals across random and protein-overlap-controlled splits.

sections.title: Uneven gains in protein-RNA affinity and mutation-effect prediction
sections.abstract: The study tests whether improved protein-RNA affinity estimates also improve average mutation effects, mutation ranking, and local prediction accuracy.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across 220 pairs, the authors report improved mean-effect accuracy but no decrease in mean-centered local error and uncertain ranking gains. In the independent set, mean-centered local error fell overall from 0.4198 to 0.3761 pKd, though one of three families had higher error.
sections.unique_caveat: Performance varies by family and metric; the small independent test cannot establish broad transfer. This paper is included outside the configured biology-category query for its direct protein-RNA focus.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It compares 11 method families, 220 mutation pairs across 20 families, and an independent test of 24 quantitative pairs from three source-matched families.

sections.title: STORM: A Lightweight Structure-Free Model for Binding Affinity Prediction
sections.abstract: STORM combines protein and molecule representations to predict small-molecule binding affinity without requiring a predicted complex structure at inference.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose similarity transfer from reference molecules as a lightweight route to affinity prediction and suggest combining historical experimental affinity data with structural and biophysical information.
sections.unique_caveat: This is an in-silico benchmark claim, not evidence of experimental hit rates or drug efficacy; performance on novel targets and scaffolds requires independent assessment.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors compare on multiple evaluation datasets and report accuracy comparable to or above Boltz-2 on those tests, with over five orders of magnitude faster training and inference.

sections.title: Micrograph B-factor estimation via Wilson statistics
sections.abstract: The method estimates and corrects a separate B factor for each cryo-EM micrograph before three-dimensional reconstruction rather than applying one global correction afterward.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that per-micrograph Wilson-statistics estimates can account for variable image decay and improve reconstruction resolution in their tests.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence comes from three datasets and specific RELION reconstructions; the abstract does not establish that the gain generalizes across targets, acquisition protocols, or pipelines.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Evaluated using three real-world EMPIAR datasets; for beta-galactosidase, the authors report a 0.2 Å resolution improvement after micrograph-level correction.

sections.title: MitoWorld: A Stochastic World Model of the Single-Cell Cycle under Genetic Perturbation
sections.abstract: MitoWorld generates single-cell image trajectories after gene knockdown and jointly models appearance changes and cell-division timing.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors model continuous image evolution with a division hazard, offering a generative tool for time-lapse perturbation screens.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is computational and limited to MitoCheck; generated trajectories do not show that predicted perturbation effects generalize to new cell types or experimental settings.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report evaluation on 325 held-out MitoCheck tracks spanning 17 knockdowns and a control, with lower FID and JEDi than their strongest baselines and near-nominal 90% interval coverage.

sections.title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics
sections.abstract: HORIZON models changes in tissue state and cell abundance while factoring out common rotation and translation in spatial-transcriptomics snapshots.
sections.claimed_contribution: The method estimates relative tissue pose and continuous tissue, expression, and abundance changes from snapshots.
sections.unique_caveat: Snapshot-derived distributions do not track the same living cells; inferred dynamics depend on sampling, alignment, and modeling assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report coordinate-perturbation simulations and improved reconstruction plus held-out-stage interpolation on four spatial-transcriptomics time courses.

sections.title: Elysium: Simulation-Free Unbalanced Schrödinger Bridges
sections.abstract: Elysium learns state transitions and population changes from destructive single-cell snapshots without simulating trajectories during training.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose direct regression objectives for an unbalanced Schrödinger bridge and report recovery of the optimum under stated assumptions.
sections.unique_caveat: Inferred population distributions and events are not direct lineage observations; simulation-ground-truth results do not independently validate biological mechanisms.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Authors report tests against simulated benchmarks with known ground truth and single-cell time courses, including biphasic drug-response dynamics.

sections.title: Unmyelinated axons alter the biological interpretation of MRI biomarkers of demyelination
sections.abstract: MRI and electron microscopy in a cuprizone mouse model indicate that unmyelinated axons contribute to white-matter metrics often interpreted as myelinated-fiber biomarkers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that short-diffusion-time axonal water fraction reflects total intra-axonal space and g-ratio estimates should include both myelinated and unmyelinated axons.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a mouse-model and imaging-method result; it does not validate a human diagnostic biomarker or establish clinical utility.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors combine diffusion and relaxation MRI with electron microscopy and report up to 8% negative bias in g-ratio estimates when within-voxel heterogeneity is ignored.

sections.title: A structure-based model of the bacterial chemosensory array reveals how the scaffolding protein CheW tunes sensory responses
sections.abstract: A structure-based lattice model tests how CheW abundance and placement could change bacterial chemosensory-array cooperativity, sensitivity, and activity fluctuations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose that CheW tunes effective coupling and predict a crossover from relaxational to oscillatory fluctuations.
sections.unique_caveat: The new dynamic signatures are model predictions, not direct observations in this study; targeted single-cell measurements are needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The model quantitatively reproduces previously reported CheW-titration effects and yields specific predictions for single-cell signaling dynamics.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.abstract: Protein-structure and interaction evaluation; cross-modal molecular prediction and reconstructed cell dynamics; molecular imaging and mechanistic models recur in the selected batch. These are corpus-level groupings, not evidence of a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.abstract: The papers motivate matched-assay validation for SCOPE, prospective MyoECG evaluation, controlled molecular assays for protein-model generalization, direct time-series tests for inferred cell dynamics, and transfer studies for micrograph B-factor correction and MRI/axon interpretation.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.abstract: The batch is notable for protein-model evaluation and methods that transfer information across measurements or infer hidden cellular states. Evidence ranges from curated experimental cases and large retrospective cohorts to computational benchmarks and mechanistic modeling; independent experimental validation remains essential.
